guide: Leonida Legend — original guides, roadmap and tracker data

roadmap.name: Story Campaign
roadmap.tip: Play the campaign in order; bank the named-mission and chapter trophies and learn the map.

roadmap.name: Strangers & Side Missions
roadmap.tip: Finish every contact strand to its final mission; eight completed strands earn silver.

roadmap.name: Collectibles & Exploration
roadmap.tip: Sweep Leonida region by region: cards, meditation spots, vehicles, areas and garages.

roadmap.name: Activities & Challenges
roadmap.tip: Ranges, races, stunts and challenges — short repeatable wins, best done fresh.

roadmap.name: Crime, Combat & Money
roadmap.tip: Robberies, heists and money systems: stage a getaway vehicle first, every time.

roadmap.name: Partner Co-op
roadmap.tip: Two trophies need your partner present for the whole sequence; plan one session.

roadmap.name: Final Clean-up & 100%
roadmap.tip: One-time moments, the 100% completion push, then the platinum itself.

trophies.name: Vice Got a Price!
trophies.guide: This is the platinum, and it unlocks automatically the moment the other 54 trophies are all earned, so there is nothing separate to grind for it. Treat this guide's seven-stage roadmap as your route: finish the story first, clear the stranger strands, sweep the collectibles, and leave the 100% completion push for last. The most common pitfall is losing track of a small counter — a few stunts, card sets or registered vehicles — so use the tracker checkboxes as you play rather than reconstructing progress at the end. If the platinum does not pop, compare your earned list grade by grade; a single bronze left in Activities is almost always the culprit. Sources: official PlayStation trophy list (name, description, grade); Exophase and PSNProfiles trophy listings, which agree on all 55 names, descriptions and grades.
steps: Earn every story trophy in Stage 1
Clear the stranger strands in Stage 2
Sweep collectibles and activities in Stages 3-4
Finish crime, co-op and clean-up in Stages 5-7
Let the platinum unlock automatically

trophies.name: Just Like Paradise
trophies.guide: Complete the mission named in the official description, Gone Fishing, which introduces the game's opening beats. Play it straight through, learn the movement, driving and cover prompts it teaches, and do not skip its tutorials — later trophies assume you know them. This is story progression — cannot be missed while completing the campaign, but do the missable moments flagged in this guide when they appear. The only pitfall is rushing past optional dialogue or pickups in the mission area, so take a slow first pass. Sources: official PlayStation trophy list (name, description, grade); Exophase and PSNProfiles trophy listings, which agree on all 55 names, descriptions and grades.

A common pitfall is wandering into free-roam grinds this early; the campaign itself is the fastest progress you can make in Chapter 1. trophies.name: You Gotta Know When to Get Off
trophies.guide: Complete the final mission of the campaign to earn this gold trophy. Before you start it, finish or deliberately postpone any open-world business you care about, top up every consumable, and make a hard manual save — finales in this series can lock you into a sequence until the credits roll. This is story progression — cannot be missed while completing the campaign, but do the missable moments flagged in this guide when they appear. The pitfall is treating the finale as the end of the hunt: most of this list is designed to be cleaned up in the post-game free roam that follows, so do not restart a save in frustration. Sources: official PlayStation trophy list (name, description, grade); Exophase and PSNProfiles trophy listings, which agree on all 55 names, descriptions and grades.

trophies.name: A Long Road
trophies.guide: Attain 100% completion as tracked by the game itself, which is why this gold sits in the final roadmap stage: nearly everything else in this list feeds it. Use the in-game completion checklist as the source of truth and work category by category — story, strangers, collectibles, activities and hobbies — rather than chasing random percentages. The efficient method is to leave this until everything else is done, then compare the game's own checklist against this tracker to find the final few percent, which are usually a handful of activities or discoveries rather than a big missing chunk. The pitfall is assuming the trophy list and the 100% list are identical; they overlap heavily but are not the same list, so trust the game's percentage screen. Sources: official PlayStation trophy list (name, description, grade); Exophase and PSNProfiles trophy listings, which agree on all 55 names, descriptions and grades.

trophies.name: Cunning Stunts
trophies.guide: Complete 250 stunts — jumps and stunt moments the game registers as you drive Leonida. The efficient method is opportunistic: take ramps, bridges and construction jumps at speed whenever your route crosses one, and keep a fast, durable car or bike as your daily driver so attempts cost nothing. Dedicated grinding works too — find one reliable jump near a safehouse, land it cleanly, loop back and repeat — but spreading attempts across the whole playthrough is far less tedious. The pitfall is assuming every airborne moment counts; only registered stunt completions advance the total, so watch for the game's own stunt confirmation before moving on. Sources: official PlayStation trophy list (name, description, grade); Exophase and PSNProfiles trophy listings, which agree on all 55 names, descriptions and grades.

trophies.guide: Try each type of activity once — the starter guide bundled with the official list counts 9 activity types, and you only need a single attempt at each, not a win. This is one of the cheapest trophies on the list if you do it deliberately: open the map's activity icons, visit one of each type, and start it once. It pairs naturally with Master-of-None-style exploration early in the game, when sampling everything also teaches you which activities feed other trophies like races, fishing and challenges. The pitfall is finishing the story with one obscure activity type never touched, so tick each type off in the tracker the first time you try it. trophies.name: The Shootist
trophies.description: Earn a gold medal in all Shooting Range challenges.
trophies.target: 42 Shooting Range challenges, gold in all
trophies.guide: Earn a gold medal in all Shooting Range challenges — 42 of them according to the starter guide bundled with the official list. Learn each range's target pattern with a relaxed first attempt, then chase gold with a steady rhythm: accuracy streaks matter more than raw speed on most ranges, and a missed shot usually costs more than a half-second pause. Work range by range and weapon by weapon, and do not leave a range on silver planning to return — returning cold is slower than finishing the job while the pattern is fresh. The pitfall is tilting after a near-miss; these challenges are short, so reset immediately and run the pattern again. Sources: official PlayStation trophy list (name, description, grade); Exophase and PSNProfiles trophy listings, which agree on all 55 names, descriptions and grades.

trophies.name: Top Fun
trophies.description: Win a Top Fun Drone Race at every location.
trophies.target: 14 Top Fun Drone Race locations, win at each
trophies.guide: Win a Top Fun Drone Race at every location — 14 locations according to the starter guide bundled with the official list. Drone races are pure route knowledge: fly the course once slowly to learn the gate order and the tight turns, then attack it, cutting corners inside gates rather than swinging wide. Wins are per location, so track which locations are done; a location you have only attempted still owes you a win. The pitfall is overcorrecting after a clipped gate — small stick inputs keep a drone fast, while big corrections bleed the time you need at the finish. Sources: official PlayStation trophy list (name, description, grade); Exophase and PSNProfiles trophy listings, which agree on all 55 names, descriptions and grades.

trophies.name: Earn Cash, Not Kudos
trophies.guide: Win 20 different races — note the word different: repeating one easy race 20 times does not finish this trophy. Spread your wins across the race types the game offers, learn each route with one exploratory run, and use a vehicle tuned for grip rather than top speed on technical courses. Races also feed the activity sampler trophy, so starting them early kills two birds. The pitfall is the rubber-band frustration of story-adjacent races; if a race keeps snatching the lead at the line, drop its difficulty by entering with a better vehicle class rather than replaying the same losing setup. Fishing challenges are timing minigames: learn the cast, bite and reel prompts in a free fishing session first, then challenge Cal when the mechanics feel automatic. The pitfall is challenging Cal the moment you meet him with no practice; a few free catches first turn this from luck into routine. The pitfall is assuming a single credit's quick failure counts; if your first attempt ends suspiciously fast with no trophy, play one complete game properly and it will register.
